title: knowledge graph: one id convention, one-time graph.json migration, loud neighbors() on unknown ids + canonical-id sensor (R17)
description: Deep-review sweep #2 (2026-07-06) MEDIUM finding R17 (F30, adversarially confirmed) — also fix #2 of the Obsidian-KB evaluation (human ruled 2026-07-06: stay on current format, fix process/data hygiene). Two contradictory live conventions: orchestrator-routing SKILL.md:668,671 mandates TASK-035-style keys + raw ISO decision timestamps; graphify SKILL.md:45-46 mandates slugs (task-035, decision-...). The live graph carries both: 25 TASK-* vs 26 task-* nodes, 12 raw-ISO vs 6 slug decision ids. neighbors() is exact-match with silent [] on unknown ids (src/knowledge-graph.js:325-352) and addNode's dup guard is case-sensitive (:216) — lookups silently miss and closes can mint split-brain duplicates. Full context: synthesis §R17 + artifacts/obsidian-kb-research-2026-07-06.md.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical id convention is chosen and documented identically in BOTH SKILL.md sites (orchestrator-routing close-protocol section and graphify skill) — they no longer contradict.

A one-time migration normalizes graph.json: all node ids and ALL edge endpoints renamed to the canonical forms; no case-variant duplicate nodes remain; migration is mechanical and committed with before/after counts.

neighbors() (and addEdge endpoint resolution) fails loudly — warn or typed throw — on ids that don't exist in the graph, instead of silently returning []; addNode's duplicate guard is case-insensitive or normalizes first; red-first specs for both.
A fast-tier sensor asserts every node id matches the canonical pattern for its type and every edge endpoint resolves to an existing node — red-proven against the pre-migration graph fixture.
